description: A fast, searchable Neovim cheatsheet covering every essential nvim command: modes, navigation, editing, text objects, search & replace, splits, tabs, buffers, macros, LSP, and more.
title: Neovim Cheatsheet
subtitle: Complete nvim command reference - searchable, fast, always free

legend.label: Normal
legend.tip: The default mode - you're here unless you've switched. Navigate, run operators, and issue commands. Enter with Esc from any other mode. Most commands only work in Normal mode.

legend.label: Insert
legend.tip: Type text directly into the buffer. Enter with i (before cursor), a (after), o (new line below), or O (new line above). Return to Normal with Esc or Ctrl+[.

legend.label: Visual
legend.tip: Select text interactively, then apply an operator. Enter with v (character), V (line), or Ctrl+v (block). Apply d, c, y, >, < to the selection - returns to Normal automatically.

legend.label: Command
legend.tip: Type Ex commands starting with :, or search with / and ?. Enter with : from Normal mode. Run with Enter, cancel with Esc. Supports tab completion for commands, files, and options.

layout.title: Modes
layout.tip: Neovim has distinct modes for different tasks. Normal is default - navigate and issue commands. Switch with i/a/o (Insert), v/V/Ctrl+v (Visual), or : (Command). Always return to Normal with Esc.

layout.title: Navigation - Basic
layout.tip: In Normal mode use h/j/k/l instead of arrow keys. Combine motions with counts: 5j moves 5 lines down. Motions also work as operator arguments - d5j deletes 5 lines down.

layout.title: Editing
layout.tip: Operators like d (delete), c (change), and y (yank) act on motions or text objects. Most edits go into the unnamed register and can be pasted with p. Use . to repeat the last change.

layout.title: Text Objects (combine with d/c/y/v)
layout.tip: Text objects describe a region by structure: words, sentences, paragraphs, or delimiters. Combine with any operator: operator + i/a + object. Example: diw deletes inner word, ci( changes inside parens.

layout.title: Search & Replace
layout.tip: Search with /pattern (forward) or ?pattern (backward). Press n/N to cycle matches. :%s/old/new/g replaces all occurrences in the file - add c flag to confirm each match individually.

layout.title: Splits & Windows
layout.tip: Display multiple buffers side by side in split windows. Use :sp for horizontal and :vsp for vertical splits. Navigate splits with Ctrl+w + h/j/k/l. Resize with Ctrl+w +/-/_/|.

layout.title: Tabs
layout.tip: Tabs in Neovim are tab pages - each holds its own window layout, not just a single file. Use :tabnew to open a tab, gt/gT to switch. A single tab can contain multiple splits.

layout.title: Files & Buffers
layout.tip: A buffer is an in-memory copy of a file. You can have many buffers open at once - :ls lists them all, :bn/:bp navigates between them. Splits and tabs are just different views into buffers.

layout.title: Marks & Jumps
layout.tip: Marks bookmark positions in a file. Lowercase marks (m{a-z}) are local to the buffer; uppercase (m{A-Z}) are global across files. The jump list (Ctrl+o/Ctrl+i) tracks everywhere you've jumped.

layout.title: Macros
layout.tip: Macros record a sequence of keystrokes into a named register. Press q{letter} to start recording, make your edits, then q to stop. Replay with @{letter} or run N times with {N}@{letter}.

layout.title: Visual Mode
layout.tip: Select text interactively before applying an operator. Enter with v (character), V (line), or Ctrl+v (block). Apply d, c, y, >, < to the selection - Neovim returns to Normal automatically.

layout.title: Folding
layout.tip: Collapse sections of a file to reduce visual noise. Requires a foldmethod (manual, indent, expr, marker, syntax, or diff). Use zc/zo to close/open a fold, zM/zR to close/open all folds in the file.

layout.title: Neovim-Specific
layout.tip: Features unique to Neovim or its ecosystem. LSP keymaps (grr, gri, grn, gra, etc.) are built-in defaults, no config needed, working on any machine or server (K hover and ]d/[d diagnostics since 0.10; the gr* family since 0.11). Note: gd is a built-in Vim motion (local declaration), not an LSP default. Plugin managers like Lazy.nvim and Mason require installation.

layout.title: Useful Commands
layout.tip: Handy Ex commands for customizing your editing environment on the fly. Make any :set option permanent by adding it to your init.lua (or init.vim) config file so it's applied on every launch.
